aisec: Unit 42 documents campaigns where autonomous AI agents automated intrusions using ordinary tools but left distinctive traces; the UK cyber agency says AI hacking mostly exploits long-neglected basic weaknesses.

New research targets LLM weaknesses: jailbreak suffix sampling, quantization-conditioned backdoors, single-bit flips, backend-model fingerprinting of agents, numeric leakage across linked prompts, and recommender criteria hijacking.

Defensive work includes attestation-based zero-trust for HPC agents, red-teaming open sovereign LLMs for prompt confidentiality, and testing whether LLMs will assist advance-fee scams; Jensen Huang deepfakes show impersonation risks.
ai: Nvidia leadership dominates headlines: Jensen Huang apologized in an all-hands, thanked the White House, denied political pressure got him rehired, and still rejects formal succession planning.

Platforms and publishers push back on generative AI: Tidal will ban AI-generated music from December 9th, the New York Times warns photographers off Photoshop's AI features, and Fincher faces AI-use suspicions.
Agents move into commerce while benchmarks show limits; OpenAI reports GPT-6 protein-design results, and Anthropic shares falling below IPO price hint at valuation pressure on AI startups.
cyber: Extortion and vishing persist: Inception launched a large SSO-credential vishing campaign tied to ShinyHunters, which claims a return after FBI arrests.

Cloud and vendor breaches hit Rackspace Spot, Radware (exposed cloud access keys), and Turnitin; the European Commission confirmed EU Academy data theft, and Colorado's myColorado app exposed about 150,000 users.
Broadcom patched critical VMware ESX and vCenter flaws including a 9.8-rated auth bypass; Volant Manticore and Webworm espionage campaigns use IPFS-based backdoors and a customized SoftEther VPN.
